operations.name: Suggest options from a website
operations.agentTask: Read the website in `sourceUrl` and write three different ways to fill the ad "Product cutout shuffle". Objective: Turn a static catalog into a short SKU/flavor ad. Visual rule: The product occupies a fixed visual anchor; surrounding color and supporting cutouts change. Beats, in order: - 0–1 s: Hero pack is visible at full useful size. Shows Brand color, Hero pack, Opening line. - 1–3 s: Product and two ingredient accents make one compact group. Shows Brand color, Hero pack, Hero pack line. - 3–5 s: Replace with second and third packs at the same anchor. Shows Brand color, Pack 2, Pack 3, Line for packs 2 and 3. - 5–6.5 s: All packs form a simple row or shallow fan. Shows Brand color, Hero pack, Pack 2, Pack 3, Range benefit. - 6.5–8 s: Hold range plus CTA. Shows Brand color, Hero pack, Pack 2, Pack 3, Logo, Call to action. Use only facts the website or pages you read state. Never invent prices, discounts, dates, guarantees or claims. When a fact a field needs is missing, write a short placeholder in square brackets, such as [offer end date]. Make the three options clearly different in angle, wording and image choice. For images, choose real, large images of this brand and product: first from the page's own images (header logo, large files, feature-page screenshots), then with an image search. A social preview card (og:image, a title on a gradient) is a last resort. Give the direct URL of the image file, never a page URL, and never an image of another brand. Use an empty string when no image fits. If image search throws because no search backend is configured, tell the user in one sentence that a SerpAPI, DataForSEO or Brave key in Settings finds better images. Then take nodetool.web.screenshot of the product's feature pages instead. Save each image you consider as an asset and look at it with view_image before you offer it. Name in the option's description any image that is only a social preview card. Write `fillOptions` as a list of three objects, `fillChoice` as "" and `fillReport` as "". Each option: - value: "1", "2" or "3" - title: a name for the direction in 2 to 4 words - description: one sentence on what it emphasizes, then the first two copy lines in quotes - image: the URL of its first image, for the option card - brandColor: the brand's accent color as #RRGGBB (buttons, links, highlights), not the page background or a theme-color that is near black or white - fields: rangeHook (Opening line: hook, at most 7 words); variant1 (Hero pack line: variant 1, at most 7 words); variant23 (Line for packs 2 and 3: variant 2, at most 7 words); rangeBenefit (Range benefit: range, at most 7 words); cta (Call to action: cta, at most 4 words) - images: product1 (Hero pack: A shot of the product alone, ideally on a plain or transparent background, so it reads as a cutout. Shown in: Hero pack is visible at full useful size. | Product and two ingredient accents make one compact group. | All packs form a simple row or shallow fan. | Hold range plus CTA.); product2 (Pack 2: A shot of the product alone, ideally on a plain or transparent background, so it reads as a cutout. Shown in: Replace with second and third packs at the same anchor. | All packs form a simple row or shallow fan. | Hold range plus CTA.); product3 (Pack 3: A shot of the product alone, ideally on a plain or transparent background, so it reads as a cutout. Shown in: Replace with second and third packs at the same anchor. | All packs form a simple row or shallow fan. | Hold range plus CTA.); logo (Logo: The brand's own logo file, such as the site header logo or its icon. Shown in: Hold range plus CTA.) Then show the Start step with `only: ["fillChoice"]` and a one-sentence note, so the user sees just the option cards. Picking one runs `apply`, which saves the images and fills the steps.
